terms.meaning: a library that handles the sliding motion and scroll state of a carousel
a reusable React helper that gives a component access to shared state
a shared data channel that passes values down to nested parts without passing them by hand

sections.name: File setup, CarouselApi, UseCarouselParameters, CarouselOptions, CarouselPlugin
sections.title: Library types and short names
sections.what: Loads the carousel library and the arrow icons, and defines short names for the library's control object and settings. Nothing is shown on its own.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the file clear names for the library's settings.
sections.watch_out: These names come from the library, so an upgrade that changes them can cause build errors.

sections.name: CarouselProps
sections.title: Carousel settings
sections.what: Lists the settings a carousel accepts: library options, extra plugins, horizontal or vertical direction, and a callback that receives the library's control object.
sections.why: Lets a parent page control the slideshow from outside.
sections.watch_out: The callback is only useful after the library is ready, so storing it early and calling it immediately can give nothing.

sections.name: CarouselContextProps
sections.title: Shared data shape
sections.what: Describes the information shared with every part of the carousel: the library's container, its control object, the scroll functions, and whether each arrow can move.
sections.why: Lets the arrows and slides read one shared state without passing settings through every layer.
sections.watch_out: Parts that read this data must sit inside the Carousel, or they receive nothing.

sections.name: useCarousel (part 1)
sections.title: Startup and arrow state
sections.what: Sets up the library with the chosen direction, keeps track of whether the previous and next arrows should be active, and provides the move-back and move-forward actions. Using the shared data outside the carousel raises an error.
sections.why: Keeps the library setup in one place and tells the arrows when they can move.
sections.watch_out: This section shows the direction applied at startup, and it does not show how a later change to the orientation setting is handled.

sections.name: useCarousel (part 2)
sections.title: Keyboard arrows and event listeners
sections.what: Lets the left and right arrow keys move the slideshow, passes the library's control object up to the page when asked, and keeps the arrow state current by listening for slide changes.
sections.why: Lets keyboard users move through slides without a mouse.
sections.watch_out: The cleanup removes only the slide-change listener, not the reinitialize listener, so that listener stays attached after the component is removed.

sections.name: useCarousel (part 3)
sections.title: Outer region and slide strip
sections.what: Draws the outer region that announces itself as a carousel and listens for key presses. Inside it, the strip holds the slides and hides anything that sticks out. The strip uses negative spacing to cancel the padding on each slide.
sections.why: Creates the sliding track, and the negative spacing keeps the slides aligned with the outer edge.
sections.watch_out: The negative spacing assumes the slide spacing comes from the item part, so changing that spacing means changing this part too.

sections.name: useCarousel (part 4)
sections.title: Single slide and previous arrow
sections.what: Draws one slide as a block that fills the full width, with padding that depends on direction. It also draws the previous arrow on the side, which is greyed out on the first slide.
sections.why: Each slide takes the full visible width, and the arrow is greyed out so users know they cannot go back.
sections.watch_out: The arrow sits outside the slide area, so a parent that clips overflow will hide it.

sections.name: useCarousel (part 5)
sections.title: Next arrow and exports
sections.what: Draws the next arrow, which is greyed out on the last slide, and makes the carousel parts available to pages.
sections.why: Mirrors the previous arrow so users can move forward.
sections.watch_out: The slides and both arrows only work inside the Carousel wrapper, which is a common setup mistake.

summary: A slideshow with left and right arrows and keyboard support, built on the embla-carousel library.
purpose: Lets a page show a set of items, such as images or cards, that the user moves through one step at a time.
why: Likely reason: built on the embla-carousel library, with shared state passed to every part so the arrows know the current position. Reason partly visible from the structure.
how: Step 1: Loads the library and sets up the shared state. Step 2: Tracks whether the previous and next arrows can be used. Step 3: Adds left and right arrow key support. Step 4: Lays out the slide strip and each slide. Step 5: Draws the previous and next arrow buttons.
inputs: Library options and plugins, an optional horizontal or vertical setting, an optional callback that receives the library's control object, and the slide items.
outputs: A slideshow on screen. The arrows enable or disable depending on whether movement is possible.
risks: The reinitialize listener is never removed when the component is removed, which can leave a stale listener running. The arrow and slide parts raise an error if used outside the Carousel wrapper.
debug: If arrows do not respond, check that the slides sit inside the Carousel parts and that there is more than one slide. If an error says the hook must be used inside the Carousel, a part sits outside the wrapper. If a slide appears cut off, check the spacing classes on the content and item parts. For listener problems, look at the effect that subscribes to library events.
